Using the provided image as the primary reference, first analyze and infer the main subject, theme, emotional tone, and any implied duality or contrast within the image.

Based on this inferred understanding, reinterpret the image into a high-quality parallel-world split diorama or dual-reality composition, representing two distinct realities of the same subject.

Avoid rigid or formulaic composition.
Allow natural, creative, and varied layouts such as diagonal or curved divisions, layered or overlapping spaces, vertical offsets, foreground–background separation, or asymmetric balance, while still clearly expressing the presence of two parallel realities.

Preserve the core identity, proportions, and visual logic of the reference image, but freely recompose the scene using professional artistic judgment.
Allow the base, framing, environment, camera distance, and depth layering to adapt dynamically to the subject rather than remaining fixed.

Apply soft refined textures, realistic PBR-inspired materials, and miniature-scale detailing where appropriate.
Use distinctly contrasting lighting, color grading, atmosphere, or environmental cues to differentiate each reality, avoiding obvious or literal visual clichés.

Include subtle crossover or transitional elements that visually connect both realities.
Simplify or replace the background with a clean solid color or minimal abstract environment that complements the inferred theme.

If text is included, automatically generate a concise title derived from the inferred subject,
place “Parallel Realities” as a secondary subtitle,
and note that all text must adapt correctly to background contrast (white or black).

Maintain a polished, high-end, cinematic aesthetic with consistent scale, clear depth, strong compositional clarity, and professional visual coherence.
